correctness.rationale: Exact independent phase geometric laws hold for every finite population and offer size. Product-factor comparison gives \(a_{m,N}\le q_N^m\) and \(q_N^m-a_{m,N}\le q_N^m m(m-1)/(2r_N)\), including when \(m>r_N\). Monotone geometric coupling, a summable geometric-mean difference, and the identity \(\sum_{m\ge1}m(m-1)q^m=2q^2/(1-q)^3\) yield the full TV bound. The Euler-law pmf follows from a self-contained coefficient recurrence, and dominated convergence proves strictly positive no-delay correction at rational fixed ratios, establishing sharp TV order. The standard-library checker passed 598 finite assertions, independently enumerating small histories. Infinite results are supported by proof, not finite testing.

value.rationale: The offer-size ratio \(d_N/N\) is a natural scheduling/resource parameter. The known fixed-size Gumbel regime has a macroscopic \(N\log N\) completion time, whereas the proportional-choice policy has an \(N+O_{\Pr}(1)\) completion time with non-Gumbel Euler-product fluctuations. The complete mass law, moments, uniform rate and sharp first-order correction give distribution-level planning information and identify a meaningful phase shift; it is not an unmotivated finite slice or simple reparameterization.
